source.title: Query Circuits: Explaining How Language Models Answer User Prompts

record.file_problem: None noted; the supplied text includes the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates circuits on IOI with a different circuit-discovery setup and faithfulness metric, and examines whether IOI query circuits remain faithful across paraphrases. It does not reproduce the original head-class analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI circuit-faithfulness, paraphrase, and shared-edge results. It also reports NFS/NDF comparisons on MMLU that bear on evaluation sensitivity. Results on arithmetic, ARC, gender-bias steering, and runtime that do not measure the listed claim versions are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study uses the IOI dataset and GPT-2 small as a benchmark for its own query-circuit methods (EAP-IG, BoN, NDF). Its circuits are EAP-IG edge sets chosen under fixed edge budgets. It never identifies the 26 heads, their seven classes or roles, backup heads, or the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria. The IOI results report how well its own discovery methods perform. The NFS-vs-NDF instability is shown on MMLU with Llama-3.2-1B, not on an IOI circuit. Appendix C.10 says NFS mostly stays within [0,1] on IOI. One finding is nearby: a dataset-averaged IOI circuit fails on single prompts, and per-prompt circuits share a core. It concerns the study's own circuits, not the claimed circuit, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors propose query circuits for single inputs and introduce NDF as a bounded metric, because NFS is unstable on general datasets such as MMLU. They show BoN paraphrase sampling finds compact circuits, e.g. 1.3% of edges giving ~0.6 NDF on MMLU. On IOI they report a shared sub-circuit across capability and query circuits. They draw no conclusion about the original IOI head circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses EAP-IG edge scoring, greedy selection, paraphrase-based BoN variants, and NDF evaluation for input-specific query circuits. It does not reproduce the original study's head-class and head-role analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to evaluation metric (NFS versus NDF), query paraphrase, number of paraphrases, and circuit-discovery method.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 small IOI, a dataset-averaged EAP-IG capability circuit (500 edges) often fails on individual prompts. Its per-query NDF is 0.00 in Fig. 8, and 0.95, 0.00, 0.10 and 0.00 in Fig. A20. Per-prompt circuits differ (Jaccard ~0.3) but share a common core (66 edges in Fig. 8; 30–50% of query-circuit edges lie in the capability circuit).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuits found by averaging over the IOI dataset do not reproduce GPT-2 small's behaviour on individual IOI prompts; per-prompt circuits vary around a shared core.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The IOI results relevant to the original head circuit do not identify the 26 heads or test their stated roles and criteria. Several IOI curve results are reported only in figures, and the paper notes that indirect-effect edge scores neglect combinatorial interactions among edges.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted results on arithmetic, ARC, gender-bias feature steering, runtimes, and larger-model scaling because they do not test the specified IOI head roles or prompt-variant claim. The GPT-2 XL IOI scaling result does not analyze the original head classes.

untested.parts: All: the 26 heads, 7 classes, roles, and faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria.
All: no name-mover ablation or backup-head analysis.
All: the GPT-2 XL IOI result reports only method performance, with no head-class analysis.
All: no comparison with the original circuit's heads.
All for the IOI circuit: no ablation-type, metric or distribution variation applied to the original circuit. Metric instability is shown only on MMLU/Llama.
All: no name-order, template or more-names variants tested for the original circuit.

missing.what: Per-query NDF of the capability circuit and of the query/paraphrase circuits at N=500 (e.g. capability 0.00 vs 0.95 across queries). Also the edge-overlap statistics: Jaccard ~0.3, and 30–50% of query-circuit edges in the capability circuit.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T2 call is overturned. The paper uses IOI only as a toy benchmark for its own method and never evaluates the Wang et al. circuit. Its 'paraphrases' for IOI are other dataset prompts, not designed prompt variants. Shared-circuit plots include heads that overlap the original circuit (e.g. a9.h9, a9.h6, a10.h0, a3.h0), but the paper assigns them no roles.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not identify or test the original 26 attention heads, their seven classes or stated roles, or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria as a package.
No ablation of main name-mover heads or test of backup-head self-repair is reported.
Scaling query-circuit experiments to GPT-2 XL does not test whether the original head classes and roles carry IOI across models, checkpoints, or tasks.
The paper compares query-circuit discovery methods and metrics, but does not establish whether other methods, ablation types, and metrics recover essentially the same original circuit.
The paper tests evaluation-metric and prompt/paraphrase sensitivity, but does not systematically vary ablation type for the original 26-head circuit.
The IOI paraphrase analysis uses word-swapped IOI variants; it does not test other templates or sentences with more names.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 Small IOI query and capability circuits at 1000 edges
reader_labels.reason: The query circuit recovers less than half of per-query performance, while the capability circuit recovers roughly 65% overall; these are partial recoveries and do not test the original head classes or criteria (R1, R2).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MMLU Marketing query circuits evaluated with NFS versus NDF
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports NFS values outside the [0, 1] range and examples where NFS and NDF give markedly different assessments, motivating a more stable alternative (R11–R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: IOI query circuits across original prompts, paraphrases, and discovery methods
reader_labels.reason: Faithfulness differs with the prompt and discovery method: the original-query circuit may fail where a paraphrase circuit succeeds, and BoN outperforms the baselines (R3–R8).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IOI word-swapped query variants and paraphrases
reader_labels.reason: The authors report successful faithful circuits from paraphrases and 66 edges shared across the capability and query-circuit variants (R8, R9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Original IOI query compared with its paraphrases
reader_labels.reason: The circuit discovered on the original query may fail to recover model performance even when circuits from its paraphrases succeed (R8).
